full_judgment:
6. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 who are the defendant Nos.16-18 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 is that Gagan Ram Malakar, Raman Ram Malakar, and Avoy Ram Malakar who are successive owners by in-heritance of the suit land and subsequently executed and registered a sale deed on 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS in favour of Jahir Ali, (the predecessor of the defendant Nos.1 and 2) receiving Taka 100 as consideration money in respect of suit land and on the same date Jahir Ali executed a registered Ekrarnama in favour of the aforesaid Gagan Ram Malakar and others in respect of the same suit land promising to reconvey the suit land to the vendors on repayment of the consideration money within, 30th chaitra, 1361 BS. The transaction was not a sale, it was a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of 7 years in accordance with the provisions of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and after the expiry of 7 years it was redeemable by operation of law. The plaintiffs on several times requested the defendants to redeem the mortgage by receiving the consideration money. But the defendants refused to comply on the end of Bhadra, 1400 BS. Hence the plaintiff is constrained to file the present suit. 

 8. The defendant Nos. 1 and 5-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The contents of defendant Nos.1 and 5-16 are almost same. It is contended by the defendant Nos. 5-16 that they purchased the land in total 29.875 decimals from Jahir Ali and his two brothers by 6 kabalas dated 1-2-1990, 16-11-1974, 12-12-1974 and 12-4-1975 and by 2 more kabalas, both dated 22-4-1975. They have been possessing the purchased lands by constructing building thereon. 

 9. The defendants Nos. 2(ka)-2(kha), 4-12 and 13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 filed written statement separately. Their case are that Jahir Ali and his brother Junayed Ali together sold 0.1225 acres to the defendant No.13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 on different dates. The defendant Nos. 4-12 purchased 0.1175 acres on different date from Jahir Ali and his brothers. The defendant No.2 purchased 0.0550 acres from Jahir Ali and his brother. 

 11. The defendant No.3 and the defendant Nos.11-22 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The statements of the defendant No. 3 is same to the statements of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 which was discussed above. The case of the defendants Nos.11-22 is that the First schedule land is a part of Fulbari Mouja. The First Schedule land had no existence in Tikorbari Mouja. Jahir Ali, the predecessor of these defendants purchased the schedule land along with other lands from the Original owner Gokul Malakar and others on 24-4-1952. Jahir All and his two brothers Jayed Ali and Tasir Ali, while possessing the suit land, Tasir Ali died. Thereafter Jahir Ali and Jonayed All sold 0.06 acres to Serajuddin, Jahir All and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 4 Jaista 3 pon,10 Gonda to the defendants No.11 on 1-2-1970 by saf kabala. Then Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0625 acres to the predecessor of defendant Nos. 13-21 on 7-11-1974. Again on 16-11-1974 Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0150 acres to the mother of defendant No.11 and grandmother of defendant Nos.13-21. Subsequently, Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0625 acres, 0.0550 acres 0.0550 acres, to defendant No.12, Abdur Rahman, the predecessor of defendant Nos.13-22 and the defendant No.11 respectively and after selling the aforesaid lands Jahir All and his brothers had no land in suit jote. 

 20. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate on behalf of defendants Nos.5-16 appellants of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 submits that the root of disputes between the parties based on the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS and the agreement for reconveyance of the said land executed on the same date stipulated a period of 3 years from the said date that is to say, the time for reconveyance expired on 30th chaitra 1361 corresponding to 24-4-1956 and the said transaction is not attracted by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He further submits that a transaction by way of out and out sale with an separate agreement to reconvay deed was not a mortgage before coming into effect of the Presidents Order (PO 88 of 1972) read with Presidents Order 136 of 1972, because of facts such transaction was not a mortgage by definition of "Mortgage" as provided in section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. He next submits that where the agreement to recovery is embodied in the same document by which sale is effected the transaction is conditional mortgage. He also submits that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to recovery which has been treated to be mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and same was not alive on 3-8-1972, the date of coming into effect of the Presidents Order 88 of 1972. He further submits such transaction is past and closed and the property involved in such transaction will not be redeemable. He finally submits that the trial court erroneously held that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and ignoring the doctrine past and closed decreed the Title Suit No.51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas of possession in respect of 0.34 acres of suit land is totally illegal. In support of his submissions learned advocate referred the decision reported in 32 DLR(AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90 and 1 BLC (AD) 164. 

 21. Mr Anwarul Azim Khair, the learned Advocate on behalf of the appellants of First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 adopted the arguments Advanced by the learned Advocate for the 5-16 defendants Nos. 5-16 appellants of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009. In addition he submits that the transaction in question of the present case is not itself mortgaged within the mischief of section 58 of Transfer Property Act. Section 58 of Transfer Property Act states about different kind of mortgage. He next submits sale deed and condition embodied in the same deed is called mortgage deed. But when the sale deed with an separate reconveyance deed, it shall come within the mischief of section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Finally he submits section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, was challenged in High Court Division by filing writ which was allowed and against which Leave to Appeal has been filed. In 32 DLR (AD) in para-11 it was discussed elaborately and was upheld. 

 22. Mr Sadananda Rana, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondents-defendants 1 and 2 of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 submits that the trial court rightly found the deed in question being NO.719 dated 24-4-1952 is a mortgage deed. Section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, has been amended by the Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 with effect from 3 August 1972, but this amendment did not touch the period of a usufructuary mortgage which  is still 7 years, nor did it effect the period of limitation for redemption suit which is 60 years. section 95A was incorporated after amendment of section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, by President Order 86 of 1972 which gives the mortgagor, the right to get his property by application to a Magistrate. This amendment gives an out and Out sale with a condition of reconveyance will still be treated. a complete usufructuary mortgage. Tits amendment says on the expiry of the period of a mortgage, the mortgagee does not restore possession of the land to the mortgagor, on the application of the mortgagor, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate will restore the possession to the mortgagor. On the other hand, for getting back possession of a mortgaged land the mortgagor need not file any redemption suit, but may get remedy by an application to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. He next submits after insertion new section of 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, any transfer of a land by an out and out sale with a condition for reconveyance shall be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding 7 years on the expiry of which the mortgagor may get back possession by an application to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. He finally submits that once a mortgage is always mortgage, and, as such, the doctrine of past and closed transaction is not applicable. In support of his submission, he referred the decision reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, 3 BLT 135, 12 MLR (AD) 26, 52 DLR (AD) 152 and 36 DLR 90. 

 23. Mr Dider Alam Kollol, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014 argued that the learned trial court without considering the evidence of the plaintiff appellants reached into erroneous decision. CS Khatian was filed by the original owner Charan Ram Malakar which was marked as Exhibit-1. But the learned court erroneously found that the plaintiff could not file documents in his support. In the plaint it was specifically mentioned that the plaintiffs were evicted by the defendants on first part of poush in 1400 BS. But the court below did not consider it. He finally submits the trial court in its judgment did not mention about the commissioners report which is totally misconceived on law. He also argued that learned court below on misconception of law found the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 is a mortgage deed. In fact that deed is within the mischief of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but it was not alive at the date of commencement of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 on 3-8-1972. So, the said transaction does not attract section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Jahir Ali became owner on the basis of deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and subsequently after selling the property 0.7 decimals remain with Jahir Ali. After death of Jahir Ali his heirs the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and plaintiff of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 became owner and they are entitled for partition of 0.7 decimals of land. 

 27. It is alleged by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and Title Suit No: 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 and defendant Nos.16-20 of Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 that the deed in question dated 24. 04.1952 was never a sale deed. It was a usufractuary Mortgage within the mischief of section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It is also alleged that the consideration money was paid and moreover it should be re-deemed after 7 years as per section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 29. The core issue in this appeal is that whether the Deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and reconveyance deed No.720 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X, X(I) are the basic documents upon which the parties claimed their respective title is complete usufructary mortgage or treated to be mortgage under section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and whether the deed in question is attracted to section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 34. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates, now we can look into the definition of "Treated to be mortgage" under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, 2[either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey,] 3[or] where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Second Amendment) Order, 1972] (President's Order No. 88 of 1972). 

 36. The learned Advocate Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, argued that an out and out sale accompanied by an agreement for reconveyance is within the purview of the Presidents Order Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 and No.24 of 1973 whereby provisions of section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been amended and a new section being section 95A has been inserted in the said Act. The Presidents Order No.88 of 1972 came into effect on 3-8-1972 (PO No.136 of 1972) and the condition giving right of repurchase having expired the sale became a past and closed transaction and on the same reason the plaintiffs are not entitled for redemption of mortgage of the suit land. In this respect he referred the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD), 233. 

 37. We have gone through the decision reported in 32 DLR, 233. It appears that in that Writ Petition No. 85 of 1974 along with good number of Writ Petitions were heard analogously. The facts of the said Writ Petition was that the respondent No.1 purchased the land from the respondent No.3 with an agreement to reconvey the said land. The agreement was dated 26-4-1963 which stipulated that the land will be reconveyed if the money is repaid within 10 years. The respondent No.3 i.e. mortgagor made an application before Sub-Divisional Magistrate for restoration of the mortgaged property under section 9(4) and 9(5) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and same was allowed on 30-3-1973. Then the said writ petitions were filed challenging the section 95A of the aforesaid Act which were made absolute and against the said judgment appeals were filed. It has been held by Appellate Division in their judgment that: "Our conclusions, therefore, are that the President's Order Nos.88 and 136 of 1972 and No.24 of 1973 are all valid legislation for affecting necessary amendments in the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and those laws cannot be attacked on the ground of ultravires. (2) any transfer of a holding or part thereof by a raiyat either way of out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and transferee acquires the right to possess and enjoy the usufruct, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of maximum 7 years and the provisions of section 95(4) and (5) shall apply to such transfers; (3) and such transfers are not to be understood in the light of the Transfer of Property Act because those are to be understood in the light of the enactment in question: (4) those transactions which are subsisting on the date of promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972 are hit by section 95A including the transaction entered into by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to recovery, made whether before or after the promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972: and (5) as for the transactions which are not alive before the promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972 they are concluded by the transactions past and closed." 

 41. Therefore Exhibit-X, X(i) coupled with section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90, 1 BLC (AD) 164 clearly proved that the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 with registered agreement deed being No.720 dated 24-4-1952 treated to be mortgage but since the transaction was not alive on 3-8-1972, at the promulgation of President Order 88 of 1972, the said transaction is not hit by section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 44. In Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 the heirs of Jahir Ali, Md Manik Mia and Sabiya Begum sought for partition in respect of 0.7 decimals of land as described in First Schedule of land and declaration for 0.02 decimals as described in second Schedule land to the plaint. Manik Mia as PW 1 in Title Suit No. 93 of 1994 in his chief stated: 

 46. The plaintiff No.1, Manik Mia, (son of Jahir Ali) admitted in his deposition that they had no title over 0.2 decimals out of 0.7 decimals. So, in this respect without praying for declaration of title, the suit for partition over 0.7 decimals is not maintainable. Moreover, Md Manik Mia, son of jahir Ali categorically stated in his chief that they sold 0.33 decimals. Thus it is evident that the second schedule land is from different Mouja which is not disputed in the suit and without declaration of title, the relief sought only for partition in respect of 0.7 decimals is not maintainable and the trial court rightly dismissed the suit. 

 50. First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 is allowed with modification that the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 is treated to be a mortgage but since the said deed is not alive on 3-8-1972 at the time of promulgation of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 is not hit under section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.
